title: Vantor names new head of U.S. government business
summary: Vantor has appointed Will Cocos as the new executive vice president and general manager of its U.S. government business, succeeding Susanne Hake. The move highlights Vantor's focus on expanding its Earth intelligence services for government clients.

title: Firefly Aerospace to fly Zeno Power radioisotope heating unit on lunar lander mission
summary: Firefly Aerospace will carry a Zeno Power radioisotope heating unit on a lunar lander mission to test its ability to help spacecraft survive the lunar night. This collaboration aims to enable future long-duration lunar missions.

title: Space nuclear programs face near- and long-term challenges
summary: Space nuclear programs are currently gaining attention but face both immediate and long-term challenges. Industry officials highlight these hurdles despite the growing interest.

title: China’s Landspace recovers booster with second  orbital launch of Zhuque-3 rocket
summary: Landspace successfully recovered the first stage booster of its Zhuque-3 rocket during its second orbital launch from the Gobi Desert. This marks another milestone in China's reusable rocket development efforts.

title: Rocket Lab to test Space Force data network connection in orbit in 2027
summary: Rocket Lab plans to test a connection to the Space Force's data network in orbit in 2027 using a Photon spacecraft. The test aims to assess interoperability with SpaceX's Space Data Network infrastructure.

title: Eoptic, Inc. Selected to Supply DeepScan™ Imaging Payloads Scheduled for Launch in 2027
summary: Eoptic, Inc. has been chosen to supply DeepScan™ imaging payloads for a launch scheduled in 2027. The company specializes in advanced multi-spectral and multi-modal imaging systems.

title: New report takes closer look at the Space Force spending surge
summary: A new report by Aerospace Corp. reveals that the Space Force's spending surge is primarily focused on classified programs, target tracking, missile warning, and command and control systems. The analysis highlights the concentration of growth in these key areas.

title: NRO to expand use of HawkEye 360’s satellite intelligence
summary: The NRO has awarded a contract to HawkEye 360 to expand the use of its satellite intelligence for locating radars, ships, and other electronic emitters. This agreement will increase U.S. government access to HawkEye 360's data for national security applications.

title: HEO to use Planet satellites for non-Earth imaging
summary: HEO, an Australian company specializing in non-Earth imaging of spacecraft, has partnered with Planet to utilize its satellite data. This collaboration aims to enhance HEO's capabilities in monitoring and analyzing objects in space.

title: New EU sanctions target leaders of Russia’s space industry
summary: The European Union has imposed sanctions targeting a key leader in Russia's space industry, specifically the head of a Roscosmos subsidiary involved in developing a synthetic aperture radar satellite system for the Russian military.

title: Astronomers discover a giant, rocky 'mega-Earth' 23 times more massive than our planet
summary: Astronomers have discovered a massive, rocky exoplanet 23 times the mass of Earth, defying previous expectations of planet formation. The 'mega-Earth' challenges current scientific models of planetary structure and composition.

title: Touchdown! Private Chinese rocket aces landing on 2nd-ever flight (video)
summary: LandSpace successfully landed its Zhuque-3 rocket, marking a significant milestone for commercial Chinese spaceflight. This was the rocket's second flight and the first time a private Chinese rocket achieved a landing.

title: Forget 'Halo' — the latest 'Futurama' episode has a ring world covered in super-intelligent rats (exclusive)
summary: A 'Futurama' episode features a ring-shaped world called 'Wheel World' inhabited by super-intelligent rats. The reference parodies the concept of ring worlds in science fiction.

title: NASA astronaut and 1st female French spacewalker remove failed ISS antenna but run out of time for replacement
summary: NASA astronaut Anil Menon and French astronaut Sophie Adenot removed a failed antenna during a spacewalk but ran out of time to install its replacement at the International Space Station on August 18, 2026.

title: Starship lives! SpaceX craft arrives at Christmas Island after 24-day ocean ordeal
summary: SpaceX's Starship spacecraft has been recovered after a 24-day ocean ordeal following its test launch and splashdown. The vehicle was towed to calmer waters off Christmas Island by SpaceX recovery teams.

summary: SpaceX successfully launched its 100th mission of the year, deploying 24 Starlink satellites into low Earth orbit. This milestone highlights the company's rapid pace of space operations in 2024.

title: Hydrogen-powered 'rocket car' tops 400 mph in record-breaking test (video)
summary: The JCB Hydromax, a hydrogen-powered vehicle, achieved a record-breaking speed of over 400 mph during tests in Utah. This marks it as the fastest hydrogen-powered car ever recorded.

summary: A total solar eclipse on August 18, 1868, led to the discovery of helium. This historical event marked the first identification of the element during a scientific observation.

summary: A beginner's guide provides instructions on using a manual telescope to observe the night sky effectively. The article emphasizes the importance of proper technique for amateur astronomers.

summary: NASA's Boeing 777 has received a new paint job and will replace the retired DC-8 aircraft. The B777 is set to begin operations from NASA's Langley Research Center in 2027.

summary: NASA Glenn Research Center has conducted decades of flight research, leading to major aerospace breakthroughs tested in real-world conditions. Their work in targeted environments like icing clouds provided critical in-flight data.

summary: The Curiosity team celebrated the 14th anniversary of the rover's landing on Mars. The milestone was marked with reflections on the mission's journey and achievements.

summary: SpaceX's Starbase production site is progressing with the assembly of multiple Starship vehicles. This indicates ongoing preparations for future missions and vehicle production.

summary: Engineers from ESA and industry partners completed a concept study for Phoenix 3, a reusable spacecraft for microgravity experiments and Earth return.

summary: Proba-3 will experience a double eclipse as the Moon crosses its field of view. This event highlights the satellite's precise alignment capabilities.

summary: ESA is preparing to study the 2026 total solar eclipse by using artificial eclipse missions and computer simulations to observe the Sun's corona, which is normally obscured by the Sun's bright disc. This approach allows scientists to gather more data than a brief natural eclipse would permit.

summary: ESA is inviting European researchers and companies to run their software aboard the Hera mission, a deep space asteroid mission. This offers a unique opportunity to test software in deep space millions of kilometers away.

summary: A drone test flight at ESA's ESTEC center in the Netherlands demonstrated a student-developed radar retroreflector technology. This marks the first use of a drone for such a payload in the space industry.

summary: ESA's Proba-3 mission will use a coronagraph to study the Sun's corona by blocking out the Sun's disk, simulating an eclipse. The mission involves two satellites working in tandem to achieve this.

summary: ESA's Industry Space Days event will host startups showcasing innovative space technologies on September 16-17 at ESA-ESTEC in the Netherlands. The event aims to foster collaboration and explore opportunities within Europe's space industry.

summary: Viasat has selected Rocket Lab to construct a small Geostationary Orbit (GEO) satellite for the Protected Tactical Satcom-Global (PTS-G) program. Rocket Lab will provide a spacecraft based on its existing platform.

summary: L3Harris Technologies appointed Sam Mehta as its new CEO and president, replacing Chris Kubasik who was forced out due to conduct issues. The leadership change was effective immediately.

title: Seraphim Space Makes Hubble Investment
summary: Seraphim Space Investment Trust is investing $30 million into Hubble Network, which is developing a satellite-powered Bluetooth network for standard Bluetooth low energy chips.

summary: Katalyst Space secured a contract from the U.S. Defense Innovation Unit (DIU) to develop deorbiting technologies. The deal highlights the growing role of private companies in advancing space debris mitigation solutions.

summary: Peru has awarded a $14 million connectivity deal to Gilat Satellite Networks, a company specializing in satellite communications. The agreement aims to enhance internet access in the country with a population of around 35 million people.

summary: Lynk and Omnispace have completed their merger, forming a new company called Elveo Mobile. The combined entity aims to advance mobile satellite communications.

summary: Conflicts worldwide have increased demand for space-based intelligence, with governments and militaries prioritizing rapid access to sovereign data. BlackSky's CTO Patrick O'Neil discusses the shifts in adoption of such technologies.

summary: The U.S. Space Force awarded contracts to five satellite manufacturers to develop a diverse multi-vendor space data network architecture. This initiative aims to enhance the military's space-based data capabilities.
